findings.title: Hardcoded SECRET_KEY found in settings
findings.description: SECRET_KEY is hardcoded in source code. Anyone with access to the repo can forge session cookies, sign malicious tokens, and bypass authentication.
findings.fix: Load SECRET_KEY from an environment variable (e.g. os.environ['SECRET_KEY']) or secret manager.

findings.title: API Endpoint relying on global AllowAny: /

findings.fix: Explicitly assign authentication and permission classes (e.g. permission_classes = [IsAuthenticated]) or require session login.

findings.title: Django ALLOWED_HOSTS wildcard enabled
findings.description: ALLOWED_HOSTS contains '*' which permits Host header poisoning attacks, cache poisoning, and password reset poisoning.
findings.fix: Specify explicit domain names or hostnames in ALLOWED_HOSTS.

findings.title: Django DEBUG set to True
findings.description: DEBUG mode is enabled. Detailed error pages expose stack traces, settings, and internal variables to users.
findings.fix: Set DEBUG = False or load from environment variable (e.g. os.getenv('DJANGO_DEBUG', 'False').lower() in ('true', '1')).

findings.title: Django DEBUG set to True
findings.description: DEBUG mode is enabled. Detailed error pages expose stack traces, settings, and internal variables to users.
findings.fix: Set DEBUG = False or load from environment variable (e.g. os.getenv('DJANGO_DEBUG', 'False').lower() in ('true', '1')).

findings.title: Flask debug mode enabled in app.run
findings.description: Flask application is launched with debug=True, enabling the interactive Werkzeug debugger which permits remote code execution.
findings.offending_snippet: app.run(host='0.0.0.0', port=5000, debug=True)  # Vulnerable: Debug mode enabled in production
findings.fix: Set debug=False or remove debug argument before deployment. Use production WSGI server (Gunicorn/Uvicorn).
